question: What changes when an employer moves its pension to an insurer?
answer: Pension risk transfer changes the legal obligor and protection regime, not merely the asset manager. The chain differs for a buy-in, where the annuity remains a plan asset and the plan continues to owe participants, and a buy-out, where the insurer becomes the direct benefit payer for transferred obligations. PBGC also states that its guarantee ends after plan assets are distributed in a standard termination. The insurer becomes responsible for annuity payments. Any later state guaranty-association protection is state-, residency-, product- and limit-specific.

sections.title: Every box in the pension-transfer lens
sections.sub: A pension transfer changes the obligor and the protection regime. Follow the sponsor, plan fiduciary and assets through annuity-provider selection, buy-in or buy-out, insurer reserves and reinsurance, participant payment, PBGC exit and state guaranty boundaries.

items.title: SEC, DOL, CMS, PBGC, FHFA, NRC, FAA and other federal perimeters
items.sub: Plan & fiduciary · Regulate named products, benefits, liquidity systems and public guarantees
kv: Reach variable products and securities, ERISA plans, federal health programs, pension guarantees, FHLBank membership, taxes, sanctions, transport, environmental and strategic-liability regimes.
Each agency owns its statute, covered entity, instrument and enforcement or payment record.
Functional federal authority is not one consolidated insurance regulator.

items.title: Employer plan sponsor and ERISA fiduciaries
items.sub: Plan & fiduciary · Own the plan decision and must act prudently for participants
kv: Govern the defined-benefit plan and decide whether and how to transfer or settle liabilities.
ERISA duties, plan documents, board or committee authority and transaction process govern.
Employer sponsorship does not make corporate assets plan assets or permit an imprudent provider selection.

Pension and retirement risk-transfer control map

items.title: Defined-benefit plan and trust assets
items.sub: Plan & fiduciary · Hold assets for accrued plan benefits before distribution
kv: Funds participant benefits and supplies premium or assets for an annuity transaction.
Plan terms, ERISA trust and funding rules, fiduciary mandates and custody determine use.
Plan assets are not employer cash, insurer assets or the actuarial liability measure.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)
Pension and retirement risk-transfer control map

items.title: IB 95-1 safest-available selection process
items.sub: Selection & transaction · Requires an objective, thorough and analytical insurer search
kv: Tests insurer portfolio, size, capital, liabilities, contract guarantees and state guaranty protection with qualified expertise.
ERISA fiduciary duties and Department of Labor guidance govern provider selection.
Ratings alone are insufficient, and a prudent process cannot guarantee that the insurer never fails.

Pension and retirement risk-transfer control map

items.title: Buy-in, buy-out, liftout or standard termination
items.sub: Selection & transaction · Different transaction forms move different obligations
kv: Selects whether the plan retains the participant promise or distributes it to an insurer for some or all participants.
Board and fiduciary action, ERISA/PBGC process, contract and settlement records determine state.
Announcement, insurer selection, premium payment, contract issue and participant distribution are separate clocks.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)
Pension and retirement risk-transfer control map

items.title: Issuing life insurer
items.sub: Insurer promise · Owns the retail policy obligation and statutory filing
kv: Writes policy liabilities, holds or controls supporting assets and files statutory reserves and capital.
Board, management and appointed actuary control company records subject to domiciliary supervision.
Group brand, parent ownership or affiliated manager does not replace the named policy issuer.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)
Life and annuity funding state; Life and annuity annex

items.title: Group annuity contract and issuing insurer
items.sub: Insurer promise · Defines the transferred payment promise and account support
kv: Obligates the named life insurer to pay transferred benefits under the group annuity terms.
Executed contract, state insurance law, reserve and account treatment govern the promise.
Brand, parent or bidding consortium does not identify the legal obligor without the contract.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)
Pension and retirement risk-transfer control map; Life and annuity funding state

items.title: Participant certificate and beneficiary record
items.sub: Insurer promise · Connects the group contract to the person owed payment
kv: Records benefit amount, form, beneficiary, address, tax and payment rights after transfer.
Plan benefit determination, annuity contract and insurer administration establish the record.
A transaction total does not establish one participant’s benefit, notice or first payment.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)
Pension and retirement risk-transfer control map

items.title: Reserve-supporting assets and capital
items.sub: Reinsurance & capital · Finances the promise but does not replace it
kv: Supports expected claims and required capital through invested assets, liquidity and surplus.
The legal owner, investment manager, custodian and regulator each control different parts of the asset chain.
Asset amount, manager affiliation or private-credit label does not by itself establish liquidity, ownership, valuation error or insolvency.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)
The Insurance Machine; Life and annuity funding state

items.title: Asset-intensive reinsurer
items.sub: Reinsurance & capital · Assumes defined liabilities and asset economics
kv: Receives premium, reserves or investment economics under coinsurance, modified coinsurance, funds-withheld or related structures.
Treaty, domicile, collateral and investment terms determine actual control and capital treatment.
Offshore location, reciprocal-jurisdiction status or large ceded reserve does not alone prove weakened security or insolvency.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)
Life and annuity funding state; Life and annuity annex; Cross-border supervision, market structure and resolution map

items.title: Pension-annuity assets, reserves and reinsurance
items.sub: Reinsurance & capital · Move insurer economics while the issuing promise remains entity-specific
kv: Supports the annuity block through reserves, general/separate-account assets and possible reinsurance.
Statutory filings, valuation, asset custody, treaty, collateral and recapture provisions govern.
Reinsurance does not ordinarily give the annuitant a direct claim against the reinsurer.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)
Pension and retirement risk-transfer control map; Life and annuity funding state; Ownership, governance and affiliate control map

items.title: State insurance commissioners
items.sub: Benefit & failure · Primary legal-entity supervisors of the business of insurance
kv: License, examine and enforce against domestic insurers; control reserves, capital, material transactions, dividends and receivership under state law.
The domiciliary commissioner controls the licensed legal entity; other states retain market and consumer authority within their laws.
State primacy does not eliminate federal securities, benefit, financial-stability, tax or public-program authority.

Big insurance monetary and government control map; Insurance source watchboard; Commercial, specialty, cyber and AI control map; Cross-border supervision, market structure and resolution map; Compulsory insurance and financial-responsibility constitution; Insurance accounting, tax and jurisdictional-location constitution; Domestic insurer failure, receivership and policy-continuity constitution

items.title: Medicaid statutory program and state contract
items.sub: Benefit & failure · Defines eligibility, benefits and managed-care duties
kv: Combines federal law, approved state program choices and contracts with delivery entities.
State and CMS control different approval, financing and oversight records.
Program authority, contract approval, capitation payment, provider payment and delivered care are separate.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)

items.title: Life and health guaranty system
items.sub: Benefit & failure · State statutory protection after specified failure trigger
kv: Coordinates limited covered obligations after impairment or insolvency under state law.
Domiciliary receivership, guaranty statutes, limits, exclusions, assessments and transfer arrangements govern.
It is not pre-failure federal insurance, unlimited protection or a guarantee of every contract feature.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)
Life and annuity annex; The Insurance Machine; Domestic insurer failure, receivership and policy-continuity constitution

items.title: PBGC plan protection and termination process
items.sub: Benefit & failure · Applies to the covered plan before distributed annuity benefits exit
kv: Administers termination filings and guarantees covered benefits in its statutory plan-insurance perimeter.
ERISA, PBGC regulations, plan status and asset distribution determine the boundary.
PBGC does not simply continue to guarantee a distributed private annuity after plan assets are settled.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)
Pension and retirement risk-transfer control map; Health and social-insurance map

items.title: State life and annuity guaranty framework
items.sub: Benefit & failure · Provides bounded post-insolvency protection after a state trigger
kv: Can continue or cover eligible annuity benefits subject to state law, limits and association process.
Insurer domicile, participant residence, contract type, insolvency trigger and statute govern.
Coverage is not uniform, unlimited, pre-failure liquidity or a federal PBGC continuation.
Research notes in the package (internal files, not linked)
Pension and retirement risk-transfer control map; The Insurance Machine

items.title: Annuity benefit payment or failure record
items.sub: Benefit & failure · Shows whether the promised retirement cash actually arrived
kv: Records scheduled insurer payment, delay, dispute, guaranty continuation or participant loss.
Contract administration, beneficiary data, receivership and guaranty processes govern outcome.
Provider selection, contract issuance and reserve booking do not prove every later payment.

A buy-in is not a participant-level novation.
PBGC protection does not simply follow a benefit into a private annuity after distribution.

catalog_context.title: How insurers invest trillions, move risk and share losses with government
catalog_context.answer: U.S. insurance runs through many separate regulators, very large insurer balance sheets, reinsurance and public loss programs that together work as one system. Each authority, company, contract and payment still keeps its own legal identity and timing.
